A.explanation: Area under a displacement-time graph has no useful physical meaning and does not give $a$. Area means multiplying displacement by time.

B.explanation: Area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement, $\Delta s = v \times t$, not acceleration.

C.explanation: Gradient of a displacement-time graph gives velocity, $v = \Delta s / \Delta t$, not acceleration.

D.explanation: Gradient of a velocity-time graph gives $\Delta v / \Delta t$, which is acceleration $a$.

hints: Start from what acceleration means: the rate of change of velocity, $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$ with unit $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
Recall that on any graph a gradient means $y$-change divided by $x$-change, while an area means $y$ multiplied by $x$.
Check which pairing gives $\Delta v$ divided by $\Delta t$: a velocity-time graph with its gradient taken.
walkthrough: Identify the definition needed: acceleration is the change in velocity per unit time, $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$.
For a velocity-time graph the $y$-axis is $v$ and the $x$-axis is $t$, so its gradient is $\Delta v / \Delta t$.
Therefore the gradient of a velocity-time graph equals acceleration, with unit $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
By contrast, gradient of displacement-time gives velocity and area under velocity-time gives displacement, so the other options give the wrong quantity.
Matching this result to the list, This is option D.
